description: The Fraser Valley Regional District has ordered anyone remaining in Boston Bar, B.C., to leave immediately due to a new fire south of the community.
title: Boston Bar, B.C., residents ordered to 'leave now' due to new, fast-moving fire

description: Alberta-based liquor businesses say they will be impacted if the United States follows through with a threat to impose 50 per cent tariffs on Canadian alcohol products next month and some are calling for the province to retaliate.
title: Alberta-based liquor businesses prepare to ‘start pivoting’ amid latest U.S. tariff threat

description: Jackie Patton, who lives nearby, told CBC News she was having lunch when she heard multiple police sirens rush into the plaza. She said about a minute later, she heard three shots.
title: 'Serious' police incident closes North Vancouver's Westview Plaza

description: At Tuesday's meeting between provincial leaders in Charlottetown, nine premiers agreed to update their rules that would allow more Canadian brewers and distillers to sell their products directly to consumers in other provinces.
title: N.W.T. and Nunavut premiers abstain from agreement on direct-to-consumer alcohol sales

description: Canada will celebrate the opening of the Gordie Howe International Bridge this week, the federal minister of infrastructure said Tuesday— but there will not be a celebration with the United States.
title: No cross-border ceremony for Gordie Howe bridge in light of U.S. trade threats: minister

description: One of Canada's major grocers has announced a new approach to competition around the land where its stores are located.
title: Sobeys' parent company vows change to practice that blocked competing stores

description: Provinces across Canada will introduce direct-to-consumer alcohol sales — a step forward in breaking down interprovincial trade barriers that prevent the free movement of alcohol across Canada.
title: 9 premiers to allow wineries, distilleries, breweries to sell directly to consumers across provinces

description: Manitoba Conservation officers Vitalii Skrynnyk and Owen Jones are relatively new to Churchill, but they already have a whale of a tale.
title: Conservation officers protect beached belugas in Churchill, Man., until tide returns

description: Mike D of the Beastie Boys is set to tour for his upcoming solo debut, Thank You. The tour, which includes shows in Toronto and Vancouver, will be the first by a member of the iconic rap trio since MCA's death in 2012.
title: The Beastie Boys' Mike D is back, and he's coming to Canada

description: NVision Insight Group Inc., an Ottawa-based Indigenous management consulting firm, has earned hundreds of thousands of dollars in sole-sourced contracts from the federal government since 2021. Lori Idlout has placed her interest in the company in a trust.
title: Nunavut MP cedes control over firm earning thousands from the government

description: CBC Sports' daily newsletter looks at the Canadian swimmers to watch at the upcoming Commonwealth Games in Scotland.
title: Commonwealth Games swimming preview: Liendo's time to shine

description: Canada has sent a star-studded team to the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, but there are fewer medals on the table for all countries.
title: Canada fields star-studded team at downsized Commonwealth Games

description: A doctor at Toronto's Hospital for Sick Children has been arrested and charged with possessing and accessing child sexual abuse and exploitation material, police say.
title: Doctor at Toronto's Hospital for Sick Children charged with possessing, accessing child sex abuse material

description: Leaders from Gull Bay First Nation, Whitewater Lake First Nation, Fort William First Nation, Anishinabek Nation, Nokiiwin Tribal Council and Nishnawbe Aski Nation are expected to speak from Thunder Bay on Tuesday about wildfires and Ontario Premier Doug Ford's response.
title: Indigenous leaders from northwestern Ontario react to premier's wildfire response

description: Ministers provide an update on the wildfire and drought situation across British Columbia.
title: B.C. officials give update on wildfire and drought situation in the province

description: Six captive belugas from Canada are now swimming in the waters of their new homes in the United States. Marineland and a consortium of U.S. aquariums helped move the first batch of whales in a long, complex process that began Monday at the closed Niagara Falls, Ont., tourist attraction.
title: 6 beluga whales from Marineland in Niagara Falls, Ont., now swimming in new U.S. homes

description: Years after Marineland closed to the public, the aquarium has started the process of relocating some beluga whales to facilities in the U.S. See how they moved the first six.
title: See how they got the belugas from Marineland to Toronto's airport, step by step

description: A Labrador family in the local service district of Norman's Bay says their family member deserved better after waiting nearly two days for an emergency medevac for care.
title: Family, friends seek answers after Labrador woman dies waiting for medevac

description: A 16-year-old has been charged with killing or injuring animals after Winnipeg police allege they found the youth holding a knife with a dead cat nearby on Monday night.
title: 16-year-old charged with killing a cat in Winnipeg

description: The search continues for a fourth day to find two young brothers who went missing in Manitoba's Nutimik Lake on Saturday.
title: Search enters 4th day for 2 young brothers who fell into Manitoba lake

description: The B.C. Coroners Service is investigating after a 67-year-old man was found dead during an open water swim event on B.C.'s Okanagan Lake this past weekend.
title: A 67-year-old died in one of B.C.'s oldest and largest open water swim events. Here's what we know

description: Surveillance pricing, where businesses use consumer data to offer different prices based on what they think each individual customer will pay, threatens to gouge Torontonians who are already struggling to afford the cost of living, says Mayor Olivia Chow. She's introducing a motion Monday to see if the city can ban the practice.
title: Toronto mayor, local councillors look to ban surveillance pricing in city

description: One of the Toronto police officers charged in the sweeping police corruption and organized crime investigation dubbed Project South pleaded guilty to two charges on Tuesday morning.
title: Former Toronto police officer Derek McCormick pleads guilty in Project South investigation

description: Wheelchair basketball player Kady Dandeneau and lawn bowler Ryan Bester will lead Canada’s delegation at the opening ceremony for the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, Scotland on Thursday.
title: Wheelchair basketball player Kady Dandeneau named Canadian flag-bearer for Commonwealth Games

description: The Canadian government has signed on to become the first observer of the U.K., Italy and Japan's program to build the next generation of stealth fighter jets by 2035. The commander of the Royal Canadian Air Force told CBC News "it's feasible to imagine a world" where Canada becomes a full partner and buys these jets in the future.
title: Canada joins global program building 6th-generation stealth fighter jet

description: Newfoundland and Labrador Premier Tony Wakeham and Quebec Premier Christine Fréchette will meet in Prince Edward Island on Tuesday to discuss ongoing negotiations to reach a new agreement for the sale and development of Churchill Falls power.
title: Liberal critic says N.L. running out of time on MOU deal as Wakeham, Fréchette meet in P.E.I.

description: Canadian researcher Margie Davenport is helping pregnant and postpartum soccer players keep playing the game they love.

description: Opposition MPs are expressing increasing frustration over the lack of details about how a deal between the U.S. and Canada to open a long-awaited major border crossing will work, with several calling on the federal government to release a copy of the agreement.

description: There are only about 380 North Atlantic right whales in the world and earlier this month, Kristinn Skulason was able to see one just out his office window in Bay de Verde, a town in Newfoundland’s Conception Bay.

description: Heather Cline and David Stanchuk say they were blown away when they were able to find the phone. They were even more surprised to find it undamaged.
title: A Sask. artist's phone fell 2 km from a plane. They found it in a canola field in 'pristine' condition

description: Friends and family are mourning Bhishma Rajyaguru, who ​​d​ied​ Saturday evening ​after ​Saskatchewan Roughrider​ Jayden Dalke crashed into his vehicle.
title: Friends, family mourn 22-year-old killed in wrong-way crash with Sask. Roughrider

description: How a joke at this summer’s Calgary Stampede surfaced bitter tensions in the Canadian Conservative movement.

description: Evacuees from Kashechewan First Nation, who have been away from their homes for more than six months, are now awaiting water testing results to learn if it’s safe to return to the fly-in Cree community.

description: Many in the N.W.T. get counselling through an Indigenous Services Canada program that offers therapy for residential school survivors and their families, the Indian Residential Schools Resolution Health Support Program. Even though federal approval to renew funding for the program came in March, patients and therapists in the program have spent weeks in limbo as renewals and new intakes for counselling offered through the program were put on hold in late May.
title: Residential school counselling pause disrupts care for N.W.T. clients, leaves providers in limbo

description: Several outdoor events that have been cancelled throughout the region this summer due to unexpected weather conditions, including extreme heat, storm warnings and wildfire smoke. Some organizers say this is changing the way they think about event planning.
title: Extreme weather is cancelling more events in Ontario. What does that mean for the future of summer festivals?

description: For years, Shelter Nova Scotia urged Halifax officials not to install a public park across from the men's emergency shelter and raised concerns about people gathering in the space late at night. Last week, a man was shot in the park.
title: Man shot days after Halifax officials asked to take security action at 'dangerous' park

description: A recent report on the Akami-Uapishku-KakKasuak-Mealy Mountains National Park Reserve says Parks Canada is operating in a “complex and highly charged context” in Labrador — and recommends the federal agency end its existing agreement with the NunatuKavut Community Council (NCC).
title: Parks Canada should axe agreement with NunatuKavut in Labrador national park, says report

description: We're looking for several people to publish their perspectives on CBC. Not the same political commentators, but real people with real stakes who are willing to share the why behind how they feel.
title: What’s the personal story behind how you will vote in the Alberta separation referendum? Share it on CBC News

description: Two Ottawa police officers quietly left the service this month after one of them was accused of sexual misconduct and the other was criminally charged for alleged intimate partner violence, CBC News has learned.
title: 2 Ottawa police officers accused of gender-based misconduct have quietly left force

description: A veterinary team from southern Ontario has driven up to Thunder Bay to provide care for cats and dogs displaced by the region’s wildfires. More than a dozen communities, including several First Nations in the northwest, are under evacuation this wildfire season. Here's what's being done to look after the animals affected.
title: Mobile veterinary clinic set up in Thunder Bay, Ont., for animals affected by wildfires

description: U.S. President Donald Trump's surprise escalation in his trade war with Canada puts renewed pressure on the premiers — most of whom have pulled American booze from liquor stores — as they descend on Charlottetown for their annual summer meeting.
title: Trump's escalating trade war puts pressure on premiers with U.S. booze bans as they gather in P.E.I.
